neighbours.label: a quantity-change verb and the magnitude after it (rise/grew/declined/cut/increased by N percent, 'up to 40%'), not static numbers
fire: After the new law, traffic deaths in the city dropped 35 percent in two years.
The company says its new engine cuts fuel use by 20 percent on long trips.
Rents in the capital have risen 45% since the start of the decade.
Switching to LED bulbs reduced our electricity bill by up to 60%.
Visitor numbers at the museum grew by 15 percent after the renovation.
Crime in the neighbourhood has fallen 30 percent since the park was rebuilt.
Online orders jumped 250% during the first months of the pandemic.
The new irrigation system lowered water use on the farm by nearly 50 percent.
quiet: In the city, about 35 percent of traffic deaths involve pedestrians, according to the report.
The company says its new engine weighs 20 kilograms and fits most trucks.
Rents in the capital take about 45% of an average worker's income.
Our electricity bill arrives on the 60th day of each billing period.
About 15 percent of visitors to the museum come from abroad.
Around 30 percent of the neighbourhood lives within walking distance of the park.
The shop received 250 online orders during its first month.
Roughly 50 percent of the farm is planted with wheat each year.

notes: Probe: percent-change sentences scored 0.28-0.67 ('increased 330%' 0.65, 'by up to 40%' 0.67, 'cut my water bill 60 percent' 0.41). 'rise sharply' with no number also scored 0.39 on ' rise', so the change verb carries it, not only the ' ' before the digits. Static numbers (a year, a page) were 0.00. Near misses are static percentages and amounts on the same topics.
